text: Prisha is hearing voices that seem real to her but no one else in her family can hear them. She tells
her doctor about the voices and that her identical twin sister was diagnosed with schizophrenia
three years ago. Prisha’s doctor diagnoses her with schizophrenia.
Outline two explanations for Prisha’s diagnosis, based on what she told her doctor. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by a situational explanation of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD),
including an example from the behavioural explanation of OCD.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one weakness of the situational explanation of OCD, including an example from the
behavioural explanation of OCD.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how exposure and response prevention (ERP) can reduce:
• Mary’s obsession
• Mary’s compulsion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one weakness of using ERP to help Mary.

text: Mary has obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). She worries that something bad will happen
if she does not check her front door is locked 20 times every night. Mary needs help with her
symptoms.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the study by Oruč et al. (1997) on association analysis of the genetics of depressive
disorder.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate the study by Oruč et al., including a discussion about reliability.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates. 
Section B: Consumer Psychology

text: Kabir is setting up a store selling clothing in a shopping mall. He wants to encourage people to
enter his store and purchase clothing.
Suggest two ways that Kabir can encourage people to enter his store, using your knowledge of
store choice, including demographics (e.g. age and gender). [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline ‘convenience’ from Lauterborn’s 4 Cs marketing mix model.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Lauterborn’s model can be applied to everyday life, such as for advertising products.
Explain one strength of using ‘convenience’ for advertising a product on the internet.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Company B has recently won an award for the easiest-to-use mobile phone so are planning
to change their slogan. Their current slogan is ‘B is brilliant’.
Explain two reasons why ‘B is brilliant’ is not an effective slogan.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one problem psychologists have when they investigate slogans.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about:
• choice blindness, and
• consumer memory for advertising including how retroactive and proactive interference
affect memory.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about:
• choice blindness, and
• consumer memory for advertising including how retroactive and proactive interference
affect memory,
including a discussion about experiments.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates. 
Section C: Health Psychology

text: People who experience chest pains sometimes delay seeking treatment from health services and
need to be encouraged to seek treatment as quickly as possible.
Suggest two ways that these people could be encouraged to seek treatment quickly, using your
understanding of reasons for delay. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline one example of a sample of children used in a study of healthy eating.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one reason why it is important to use children in psychological research on healthy
eating.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how Mr Sharma could use fear arousal to encourage his students to wash their
hands correctly. Your answer must be ethical.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one practical problem that Mr Sharma might have with implementing what you have
suggested in part (a).

text: Mr Sharma is a teacher in a school who is concerned that his students are not washing their
hands correctly.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about:
• biofeedback to manage stress, and
• stress inoculation training to prevent stress.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about:
• biofeedback to manage stress, and
• stress inoculation training to prevent stress,
including a discussion about determinism versus free-will.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates. 
Section D: Organisational Psychology

text: Yash is the sales manager of a chocolate company that sells chocolate online. He wants to expand
their sales into grocery stores within the next month.
Suggest a SMART goal Yash can set for his sales team to expand their sales into grocery stores
within the next month. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the nomothetic approach, including an example from Deci and
Ryan’s self-determination theory of motivation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one strength of using a nomothetic approach to understand motivation at work, using
Deci and Ryan’s theory as an example.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Samir is a manager in a bicycle factory. He has noticed several acts of sabotage, for example,
some of his workers have been leaving the factory before their shift has finished without
permission. Samir has also seen one employee putting some bicycle parts belonging to the
factory into their car.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Using your knowledge of the study by Giacalone and Rosenfeld (1987):
Outline one reason that a worker at Samir’s factory could give for one of these acts of
sabotage.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest one way that Samir could reduce sabotage at his factory.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one weakness for the way to reduce sabotage that you have suggested in part (a)(ii).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about:
• Kouzes and Posner’s Leadership Practices Inventory, and
• Kelley’s five followership styles.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about:
• Kouzes and Posner’s Leadership Practices Inventory, and
• Kelley’s five followership styles,
including a discussion about psychometrics.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates.
